items.followUp: What is volatile memory? Give one example.

rubric.why: The answer must explain that non-volatile memory retains its contents without power.
rubric.description: States that it retains data when power is off.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing retention of data without power.

rubric.why: An example helps identify a type of non-volatile memory.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an example such as ROM or flash memory.

modelAnswer: Non-volatile memory retains its data even when the power is switched off.
Examples include ROM and flash memory.

items.followUp: Prepare the truth table for the AND operator.

rubric.why: The output of OR is 0 when both inputs are 0.
rubric.description: Gives the correct output for inputs 0, 0.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the row A=0, B=0, output=0.

rubric.why: OR gives an output of 1 whenever at least one input is 1.
rubric.description: Gives the correct outputs for the other three input combinations.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for all three remaining rows being correct.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of a firewall?

rubric.why: Encryption changes readable information into a form that cannot readily be understood.
rubric.description: Explains that encryption converts readable data into coded or unreadable data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the conversion of plaintext into ciphertext or coded data.

rubric.why: The main purpose is to protect information from people who are not authorized to read it.
rubric.description: States that encryption protects data and/or that it can be read again using the correct key.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the security purpose or the role of a decryption key.

modelAnswer: Encryption converts readable data (plaintext) into coded, unreadable data (ciphertext).
It protects information from unauthorized access; the data can be restored using the correct decryption key.

rubric.why: Phishing uses deceptive communication or a fake site to trick its target.
rubric.description: Describes phishing as a deceptive message, website, or attempt to impersonate a trusted source.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the deceptive method.

rubric.why: The attacker aims to obtain valuable private information.
rubric.description: States that the attacker tries to steal personal or sensitive information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the information phishing attempts to obtain.

modelAnswer: A phishing attack is a deceptive attempt, often using a fake email or website, to trick a person.
Its purpose is to steal sensitive information such as passwords or bank details.

items.followUp: Name one example of a guided communication medium and one example of an unguided medium.

rubric.why: Communication media are commonly classified as guided and unguided.
rubric.description: Names the two main types of communication medium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for guided and unguided, or wired and wireless.

rubric.why: These are valid examples of guided media.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of a guided medium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any valid guided-medium example.

modelAnswer: The two main types of communication medium are guided (wired) and unguided (wireless).
Examples include twisted-pair, coaxial, or fibre-optic cable for guided media, and radio waves or microwaves for unguided media.

items.followUp: What is the use of POP3?

rubric.why: SMTP is the protocol used to send email.
rubric.description: States that SMTP is used to send or transfer outgoing email.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its email-sending function.

rubric.why: The question asks about the named protocol, so expanding SMTP completes the answer.
rubric.description: Gives the full form of SMTP.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct full form.

modelAnswer: SMTP is used to send or transfer outgoing email over a network.
SMTP stands for Simple Mail Transfer Protocol.

items.followUp: What is meant by the data link layer?

rubric.why: The physical layer is the lowest layer of the OSI model.
rubric.description: Identifies the physical layer as the lowest OSI layer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating its position in the OSI model.

rubric.why: This layer handles the transmission of bits over the physical connection.
rubric.description: Explains that it transmits raw bits through a physical medium or defines the physical transmission signals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for its bit-transmission function or physical transmission specifications.

modelAnswer: The physical layer is the lowest layer (Layer 1) of the OSI model.
It transmits raw bits over the physical medium and deals with the physical signals and connection.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of the href attribute in an HTML tag?

rubric.why: Attributes provide extra information about an HTML element.
rubric.description: States that attributes give additional information about HTML tags or elements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the purpose of attributes.

rubric.why: Attributes are written in the opening tag, generally as a name-value pair.
rubric.description: States where or how an attribute is written, or gives a valid attribute example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the name-value form, placement in the opening tag, or a valid example.

modelAnswer: Attributes provide additional information about an HTML element.
They are written in the opening tag as name-value pairs, for example: <a href="page.html">.
